name: Devon Energy Corporation
reason: Oil and gas E&P whose earnings are set by commodity prices (EBIT margin swung from -13.6% in 2020 to 43.3% in 2022; adjusted EPS 3.92 is 0.47x the 2022 peak) with 10y EPS CAGR of only 4.5% and shares up 4.5%/yr from the WPX merger.

name: American International Group, Inc.
reason: Decade-long restructuring (Corebridge separation, revenue -7.5%/yr over 10y, avg ROE 4.3%) makes the remaining commercial P&C book hard to underwrite; EPS growth has come mainly from buybacks (2.5x FCF) and EPS sits at 1.0x its 10y high in a firm pricing cycle.

name: M/I Homes, Inc.
reason: Well-run, low-leverage homebuilder (net debt/EBITDA 0.7x) but earnings are driven by the housing and mortgage-rate cycle (EBIT margin 7% pre-2020 vs 16% in 2022, consensus FY1 EPS -26.5%) with no durable moat; a cheap-but-ordinary cyclical.

name: A. O. Smith Corporation
reason: Leading share in a consolidated North American water-heater/boiler market driven largely by replacement demand, with 10y avg ROIC 20.8%, net cash (net debt/EBITDA 0.01x), FCF conversion 1.05x and adjusted EPS compounding 9.3%/yr; caveats are EPS at 1.0x 10y high with margin at 91st pctile, China weakness and a 22% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap.

name: ManpowerGroup Inc.
reason: Staffing business in structural decline (adjusted EPS 2.97 = 0.33x the 2018 peak, EBIT margin 1.7% vs 3.9% max, 10y EPS CAGR -5.8%) with net debt/EBITDA 3.1x and AI/automation disintermediation risk.

name: Tapestry, Inc.
reason: Coach brand momentum has pushed EBIT margin to a 10y high of 23.9% (100th pctile) and EPS to 1.0x its peak, but fashion-brand demand is hard to forecast 5-10 years out and the Kate Spade/Stuart Weitzman acquisitions produced impairments (adjusted EPS ~110% above GAAP on 5y avg).

name: Churchill Downs Incorporated
reason: Kentucky Derby is a unique asset, but growth has been bought with acquisitions (acq/FCF 2.65x over 10y) and leverage (net debt/EBITDA 5.0x), with EBIT margin at a 10y high and historical-racing machines exposed to state regulatory risk.

name: Mueller Industries, Inc.
reason: Excellent capital allocator with net cash and 21% avg ROIC, but EPS jumped from ~0.45 (2015-19) to 3.43 as EBIT margin rose from ~7% to 21% on copper prices and fabrication spreads; EPS at 1.0x 10y high makes the sustainable earnings base unforecastable.

name: Newmont Corporation
reason: Gold miner whose earnings are set by the gold price (EBIT margin 46.9% vs 10y avg 20%, 100th pctile; EPS at 1.0x 10y high) with shares up 7.9%/yr from the Goldcorp and Newcrest deals and 10y avg ROIC of 4.4%.

name: Trinity Industries, Inc.
reason: Capital-intensive railcar lessor/manufacturer with net debt/EBITDA of 7.8x, negative 10y FCF conversion (-1.7x), avg ROIC 2.7% and adjusted EPS still below 2015 (3.14 vs 5.08); consensus FY1 EPS -29% as the railcar cycle turns.

name: AGCO Corporation
reason: Farm-equipment maker tied to the ag-commodity and farm-income cycle (adjusted EPS 5.28 = 0.34x the 2023 peak, 10y EPS CAGR 5.0%) and a distant number three to Deere and CNH; no durable specialness.

name: Morgan Stanley
reason: The wealth-management pivot and management are strong (10y EPS CAGR 15.5%, 8/10 years >=7%), but earnings remain heavily driven by capital-markets activity and asset levels, and EPS is at 1.0x its 10y high after a strong trading and banking year.

name: Tecnoglass Holdings Inc.
reason: Low-cost Colombian architectural glass maker with strong historic ROIC (14.6%), but sales depend on the Florida construction cycle and US tariffs, EBIT margin has fallen from 32% (2022) to 22.9%, consensus FY1 EPS is -28% and shares rose 4.9%/yr over 10y.

name: German American Bancorp, Inc.
reason: Conservative Indiana community bank, but adjusted EPS grew only 5.5%/yr over 5y (4/10 years >=7%) while shares rose 6.3%/yr from stock-funded acquisitions (e.g. Heartland BancCorp); good but no specialness or route to >=7% organic EPS growth.

name: Federal National Mortgage Association
reason: Value of the common depends on a binary political outcome (exit from conservatorship and treatment of Treasury's senior preferred and warrants); reported EPS was ~0 for 2019-22 and the 1.3x NTM P/E is not meaningful for common holders.

name: Allstate Corporation
reason: Personal auto/home insurer with a volatile underwriting record (EPS -0.97 in 2022, 34.83 in 2025 at 1.0x 10y high after a hard-market rebound) and consensus FY2 EPS -21.9%; catastrophe and auto severity swings make 5-10 year earnings hard to forecast.

name: Credit Acceptance Corporation
reason: Subprime auto lender whose earnings depend on the consumer-credit cycle (EBIT margin 47.6% in 2025 vs 72-79% history, EPS 0.66x 2021 peak) with net debt/EBITDA 5.2x and ongoing CFPB/state AG litigation risk.

name: Fiserv, Inc.
reason: Core-processing and Clover franchise, but the 2025 guidance reset (consensus FY1 EPS -16%, LTG 3.4%) amid Clover and fintech competition, net debt/EBITDA 3.3x, acquisition-driven history (acq/FCF 0.72x) and an ~80% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap make the earnings path hard to forecast.

name: Community Trust Bancorp Incorporated
reason: Conservatively run Kentucky community bank (no buybacks or acquisitions, ROE ~11%) but adjusted EPS grew 7.7%/yr with only 3/10 years >=7%, in a slow-growth Appalachian footprint and at 1.0x its 10y EPS high on a rate tailwind; good but not special.

name: H.B. Fuller Company
reason: Adhesives maker whose growth has been acquisition-led (acq/FCF 1.67x over 10y) with net debt/EBITDA 3.6x, 10y avg ROIC of 4.5% and 10y EPS CAGR of 6.6%; margin at 91st pctile after raw-material relief.
